analyzed_vuln.description: `DngOpcodes::OffsetPerRowOrCol<S>::apply` uses the absolute image coordinate `S::select(x, y)` directly as an unchecked index into attacker-sized `deltaI`/`deltaF`. The parsed delta count is only checked against the remaining byte-stream length; it is never validated against the opcode ROI and pitch. For DeltaPerColumn (`SelectX`), a column coordinate can therefore exceed `deltaF_count - 1`, producing the reported 4-byte heap-buffer-overflow. The index should correspond to the delta ordinal within the ROI (accounting for ROI origin and column/row pitch), and construction should reject a delta count inconsistent with the number of selected columns/rows.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A TIFF/DNG reaches `DngDecoder::handleMetadata` with an OpcodeList containing opcode 11 (DeltaPerColumn). The opcode supplies an ROI/column pitch that makes `PixelOpcode::applyOP` visit an x coordinate whose current absolute value is at least the supplied delta count; a nonzero ROI left edge or column pitch greater than one can create this mismatch. The PoV supplies a valid in-image ROI and enough bytes for its declared, undersized delta vector, so parsing and `setup()` succeed; during decoding, `applyOP` forwards the visited absolute x coordinate to `OffsetPerRowOrCol<SelectX>::apply`, which reads `deltaI[x]` (for this 16-bit image) beyond the heap allocation. The analogous unchecked logic also exists for float data and row selection, but this PoV specifically triggers the 16-bit DeltaPerColumn path.
